notes: Conceptual cartoon metaphors, not literal incident architecture. Distinct boxes are different npm packages, not a package or victim count.

images.prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: tall portrait 2:3 hand-inked cartoon panel for the left 38 percent of a conference slide explaining Shai-Hulud npm worm propagation. Input image is a style, recurring-character and palette reference, not an edit target. Keep the same confident ink outlines, restrained halftone, dark petrol industrial workshop, warm amber lamps, kraft paper, burgundy wax, and small cunning coral segmented worm in a black wool cap. Create a NEW composition in which it is immediately obvious that OTHER DIFFERENT npm PACKAGES are being infected, not many copies of one package. One initial orange npm parcel is open near the upper center; the worm operates a brass publishing press using a borrowed gold key. Three outgoing conveyor branches carry clearly DIFFERENT package cartons: a very tall narrow teal carton, a small flat cream carton, a wide burgundy rectangular carton, and a squat orange cube. Vary dimensions and package design strongly, while every main carton has a crisp small RED LABEL carrying the exact familiar WHITE lowercase npm wordmark 'npm'. Do not add any other text or package names. Show the compromise newly appearing INSIDE the different downstream cartons: a small coral worm tail emerging from the teal carton, small red worm eyes peeking from the cream carton, and another little red worm newly inside the open burgundy carton. Connect the original infection to the packaging/publishing mechanism through a restrained coral trail running along actual machinery; no floating cyber arrows or diagram grid. The important visual relationship is one compromised publishing identity spreading malware to several distinct npm packages which go to other workstations. Strong legible silhouettes at small projection size, leave edge margins for portrait crop, focus on the different infected boxes more than the worm's face. No hoodie hacker, human foreground, padlocks, shields, fake code, binary wallpaper, shiny 3D rendering or random neon effects. Preserve the existing slide's cartoon craft and warmth.

Use case: illustration-story. Asset type: tall portrait 2:3 editorial cartoon panel for the left 38 percent of a technical conference slide about PERSISTENT REMOTE ACCESS after a malicious npm package has been removed. Input image is a comic STYLE, recurring-character and palette reference, not an edit target. Make a much CLEARER visual metaphor of a BACKDOOR than a hidden lever inside gears. Same bold hand-inked outlines, restrained halftone, dark petrol machinery, warm amber lamps, kraft parcels and burgundy details. Central subject is a working legitimate automation cabinet/workstation seen in strong three-quarter cutaway perspective. Its normal FRONT has an ordinary computer terminal, a cream workflow ticket being read, and a small muted sage running light. On the cabinet's SIDE/REAR a conspicuous small SECOND DOOR has been secretly cut and hinged into the steel casing; this back door stands ajar, hidden from the front operator's view. Through it a small cunning coral worm in a dark wool cap reaches an additional brass control handle that can steer the same running machine. A separate sturdy cable from this hidden control passes through the rear opening toward an outside remote control box, making the durable control route unmistakable. At the bottom foreground an EMPTY, DISCONNECTED orange npm carton lies discarded, with a small recognizable white 'npm' wordmark on a red label. That parcel is no longer connected to anything, while the rear route is visibly still connected to the active machine. The message must be obvious without decoding symbols: remove the package and the attacker still has another way in. One strong open-door silhouette, machine continues working, small character integrated rather than a huge mascot portrait. No human hacker, no padlocks, no glowing shield, no binary streams, no neon grid, no fake code, no labels except the single npm wordmark, no fire or destruction, no photorealism or glossy 3D.
